description: More than just a team, we're a group of curious minds who turned a shared challenge into an unforgettable adventure! We came together with different skills, ideas, and backgrounds, but along the way, we found friendship, laughter, and a little family. From brainstorming crazy ideas to bringing RENOVA to life, every step became a memory worth keeping. We dream big, create together, and explore beyond limits. One team, many minds, countless memories! ♡
summary:
Renova is Latin for "make new". We built a game about starting over somewhere new: Mars.

You land with four crew, a few days of food, water and air, and a pile of building materials. Earth is minutes away by radio and months away by rocket, so everything after that has to come from Mars itself: ice, rock, thin air and weak sunlight.

RENOVA is a colony-building game for kids aged 7 to 12. You dig ice and melt it into water, wash the poison out of Martian soil so you can grow food, split carbon dioxide to make oxygen, and bury your homes under regolith to keep out radiation. Every choice costs something. Power you spend on a smelter is power your oxygen plant doesn't get at night.

We used real NASA data wherever we could. Solar flares in the game come from NASA's DONKI records, radiation levels come from what Curiosity measured on Mars, and the radio delay to Earth is worked out from where the two planets really are today.

Our hope is simple: a kid who keeps a colony alive for a few sols will understand why living on Mars is hard, and maybe want to help solve it.
details:
GAME OVERVIEW

Game Concept

RENOVA is a colony-building game set on Mars. You start with a landing pad and a few crew, and you have to build everything they need to stay alive.

Gameplay & Player Journey

Fourteen short missions take you from your first solar panel to a working colony. Mines feed conveyor belts, belts feed factories, and factories turn raw rock and ice into water, bricks, metal, food and air. A field manual explains each step, and the science behind it, in plain language.

Core Colony Systems

Four things keep the crew alive:

  • Food: greenhouses grow crops from clean soil and water, under LED lights.
  • Water: ice drills dig up frozen water and melters turn it into liquid.
  • Energy: solar panels only work in daylight, so you need batteries for the night and pylons to carry power.
  • Radiation protection: habitats need a thick regolith shield nearby, or the crew gets sick.


REAL-WORLD CHALLENGES & GAMEPLAY DESIGN

Understanding the Challenges

Living on Mars isn't just about building things. There's no air to breathe, the soil is toxic, the sunlight is weak, and help from Earth takes months to arrive.

Translating Challenges into Gameplay

We turned each of these into something you deal with while playing:

  • Limited resources: you start with very little, and everything else has to be mined or made.
  • Solar flares and dust storms: they're based on real NASA records. A storm warning gives you seconds to get the crew to shelter.
  • Talking to Earth: supply ships have to be ordered ahead of time, and your messages take as long to arrive as real radio signals do today.

Strategic Trade-offs

There is never enough power or material for everything. Do you build the greenhouse first or the oxygen plant? Players learn fast that every choice has a cost.

DESIGN & TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENT

Visual Design & Art Direction

The art is isometric pixel art, all drawn in code. The buildings are based on real mission hardware: inflatable habitats, ice drills and a MOXIE oxygen plant.

User Interface & Experience

The screen is built around four things:

  • Top bar: crew, health, power, water, food and air, each with how fast it's going up or down.
  • Build bar: buildings sorted into colour-coded groups, like orange for mining and blue for power.
  • Power view: shows exactly which buildings are connected to the grid.
  • Field manual: chapters on how to play and on the science behind each building.

Branding & Web Experience

We designed the logo, the website and the game to feel like one project.

Tools & Technologies

  • Design: Figma, Adobe Illustrator.
  • Development: TypeScript, Phaser 3 game engine, HTML5 Canvas pixel art, NASA data (DONKI, Curiosity RAD, OSDR, Mars Trek, JPL).
  • Website: Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS.
  • Deployment: Vercel, auto-deployed from GitHub https://github.com/Itz0xAkira/renova. Live at https://renova-azure-two.vercel.app/play

EDUCATIONAL VALUE & INTENDED IMPACT

Learning Through Gameplay

Instead of reading that Mars soil contains perchlorate, you have to build a soil washer before anything will grow. The science sticks because the game won't let you skip it.

Skills & Learning Outcomes

Players practise:

    • Thinking ahead: setting up power before night falls.
    • Sharing scarce resources: splitting a little power or material between several needs.
    • Fixing things that break: sorting out a jammed belt or a dark grid.
    • Long-term thinking: weighing what you need now against what you'll need later.

Target Audience

RENOVA is made for kids aged 7 to 12, the age group this challenge is for. It's also simple enough for anyone curious about Mars to pick up.

Intended Impact

We want kids to finish a game of RENOVA knowing a bit more about Mars, and wanting to know more.
